VA Invention Links — National Map FedRIM

FedRIM: Federal Research and Innovation Mapped. FedRIM is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or any other government agency. Every VA research site, the universities, hospitals and companies its inventions connect to. Public sources only (USPTO assignment records, PubMed, NIH RePORTER, ClinicalTrials.gov), and, as layers, the contracts and awards its centers funded (USAspending, SBIR.gov).
How to read it: think of each VA medical center as an airport and each line as a route to a university, hospital or company. A thick line means many patents on that route. The color says what kind of tie it is. Blue lines were assigned to VA and the partner by the inventors. Click any dot or line to see the records behind it.
On the globe: drag to spin and scroll or pinch to zoom. Use the Tilt slider (top-left of the globe) to lean the camera and look across the land. On a phone, move two fingers up or down together to tilt, pinch to zoom, and twist to turn. The blue pillars are VA sites: the taller the pillar, the more linked items under the current filters. Ties with no separate place to draw to show as small colored loops beside the pillar.

Loading the 3D globe…
No geography: each VA site sits among its partners, pulled together by shared records. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. Click a dot or line for the records behind it.
0°
Right-drag (or Shift-drag) on the globe tilts and turns the camera; drag up to lean in. While tilted: drag to move, scroll to zoom. “Globe” goes back to the spinning globe.
Counts follow the filters on the Map tab. Click a row to open that site on the map. Hover a column heading for its meaning. Each record counts once: “By inventors”, “Transfer” or “After issue”, by the first assignment that gave VA its interest. A blank ORD project-year count means RePORTER files that site's awards under a generic “Veterans Health Administration” name.
